definition: The Requirements Modeling Framework (RMF) is an open-source software framework for working with requirements based on the ReqIF standard.
details: RMF consists of a core allowing reading, writing and manipulating ReqIF data, and a user interface allowing to inspect and edit request data. RMF is the first and, currently, the only open-source reference implementation of the ReqIF standards. Noteworthy is the fact that RMF has already been deployed in the ProStep ReqIF Implementor Forum in order to ensure the interoperability of the commercial implementation. Since 2011 there have been reports in the German and in the international press about RMF.

explainer.lead: RMF is an open-source framework for reading, writing and editing requirements data in the ReqIF standard. It matters as the only open-source reference implementation of that standard.

tiers.eli5: A free toolkit for opening and editing a standard file format for engineering requirements, so different tools can share the same data.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to inspect and manipulate ReqIF files without a commercial tool, and it has been used to check interoperability of commercial implementations. A pitfall is reliance on a single reference implementation for a standard whose commercial support varies.
tiers.paperLevel: Comprises a core for reading, writing and manipulating ReqIF data plus a user interface for inspecting and editing it. It is the first and currently only open-source reference implementation of ReqIF.

explainer.example: A team loads a supplier's ReqIF requirements file into RMF's interface to review and edit entries before exchanging it back.
